stepNotes.1: The unit exposes scheduling contracts and one entry point, with workflow adaptation kept in a separate production consumer.
stepNotes.2: Inputs cross an injected-executor and observer-callback boundary; the module itself performs no provider, process, network, credential, or file access.
stepNotes.3: Both scheduling paths retain positional completeness, distinguish terminal statuses, forward parent aborts, and remove their registered listeners.
stepNotes.4: Batch slices and the inflight launch guard cap active children, while summary scans and result backfill remain linear in request size.
stepNotes.5: Scheduling and result normalization stay independent of workflow authorization, persistence, artifact creation, and Bus delivery.
stepNotes.6: Unexpected scheduler rejection, executor failure, and observer failure are normalized or logged, with timers and parent listeners released explicitly.
stepNotes.7: Three focused suites cover concurrency, cancellation, merge thresholds, stable ordering, events, metadata propagation, and workflow state integration.
stepNotes.8: The ledger contains no accepted item, and the reread found no reproducible defect; delayed abort rejection remains a contract-edge test opportunity.
stepNotes.9: The targeted run passed 33 tests across 3 files, and the core package typecheck passed.
